status: exploratory; no identification claim; no outcome-ledger count
exposure_before_freeze: Palestine Open Maps home page, about page, layer list and sheet index (metadata only) were read.
Two 256-px tiles of the 1:20,000 layer near Kh. Qumran (z15, z16) were downloaded to probe the maximum zoom; they were not viewed.

The sheet-index bounding box of sheet 19-14 was compared with the Palestine-grid corners converted by pyproj: the index box lies about 165 m east and 30 m north of the converted corners. This hints at a datum offset in the published georeferencing. It is metadata, not a measured residual, and it changes no rule below.
No tile, scan or thumbnail of any sheet was viewed before this plan was frozen.

source.name: Palestine Open Maps (Visualizing Palestine)

raster_layer.credited_source: National Library of Israel; Survey of Palestine

source.sheet_downloads: Per-sheet JPEGs are linked on Dropbox shared-folder URLs (/sh/). www.dropbox.com/robots.txt disallows /sh/ for generic agents, so they are not fetched. The owner's Drive holds 16 of them; the Drive tool returns base64 only, which is too large for this session, so they are not fetched either.

vector_layer_1940s.licence: ODbL 1.0 (PalestineOpenMaps and contributors), per data.palopenmaps.org/copyright and /api/capabilities
vector_layer_1940s.use: optional QA cross-check of my readings only (C3 below); no ODbL row is copied into features.csv or names.csv

source.terms: Maps: public domain under the UK Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1998, as stated on palopenmaps.org/en/about. Vector data: ODbL 1.0. Scans stay out of the repository; tile hashes are recorded instead.

reference_imagery.name: Esri World Imagery (the 'Satellite imagery, 2025' basemap that Palestine Open Maps uses)
reference_imagery.use: read modern coordinates of a few sharp features (controls and landscape state); no image is stored in the repository
reference_imagery.assumed_error_basis: INFERENCE: not measured here; typical for commercial orthomosaics; stated so that it can be replaced by a field GNSS value

frames.grid: EPSG:28191 Palestine 1923 / Palestine Grid (= Old Israel Grid of WBADB with 1,000,000 m removed from the northing; = EPSG:28193 minus 1,000,000 m N)
frames.conversion: pyproj Transformer EPSG:4326 <-> EPSG:28191, always_xy, PROJ default operation; the operation name and pyproj/PROJ versions are written into every output
frames.output: WGS84 latitude and longitude (EPSG:4326), 6 decimals, plus EPSG:28191 metres

edition_note: The tile layer shows one edition per sheet. Where Palestine Open Maps lists two files (19-13, 19-14), the served edition is recorded as 'not determined' unless the tiles themselves show it.

windows.rule: One coding window per place: a circle around the places_v2 point. Radius 1.0 km if sigma_km <= 0.5; 1.5 km if sigma_km > 0.5. Jerusalem places use 0.6 km because the sheet is dense there. Overlapping windows on one sheet are coded once.

legend.note: The marginal legend is not in the tile layer and no full sheet is fetched, so classes are coded from printed words and abbreviations and from unambiguous symbols only. A symbol I cannot name is coded 'symbol_unidentified'.

classes.spring: label Ain/ʿAin/Sp./Spring, or a spring symbol with such a label
classes.cistern: label Cis./Cistern/Bir where the map marks it as a cistern
classes.well: label W./Well/Bir where the map marks it as a well; 'Bir' with no distinguishing symbol is coded well_or_cistern
classes.well_or_cistern: Bir/B. without a symbol that separates the two
classes.aqueduct: label Aqueduct/Aqd./Channel/Qanat, or a drawn channel so labelled
classes.road: a drawn road or track, coded once per named or classed segment near a place
classes.built_up: a built-up area, village, camp or building cluster drawn as such
classes.landform: a hill, ridge, cliff or plain name: Jebel/J./Ras/Qarn/Tal'at/Dhahr/Sahl/Buqeiʿa/Mintar
classes.locality: a land or locality name with no feature class (Ard, Hawd, Marah, Khallet, etc.)
classes.other: anything else printed (police post, pumping station, trig point, boundary stone)
classes.symbol_unidentified: a symbol whose meaning I cannot fix without the legend

coding_rules: Code every printed label and every symbol of a legend class inside a window. Cadastral parcel and block numbers are not coded.

name_as_printed: the Latin-script text exactly as printed, abbreviations kept. name_translit: the same name in a normalised scholarly transliteration (my reading, INFERENCE). arabic_script: only where the name is common and the reading is unambiguous; labelled INFERENCE (the sheets print Latin script).

Position: the symbol if the label has one; otherwise the label's first letter or centre, recorded in anchor_kind. Pick error: 15 m for a point symbol, 40 m for an area feature's centre, 100 m for a label with no symbol.
Measured position error = sqrt(pick error^2 + sheet ground residual RMS^2), where the sheet ground residual RMS comes from check G2 after the correction chosen under 'placement'.
Silence is not absence: a feature not printed is not coded and not inferred absent.
A 1:20,000 symbol cannot date a feature. No period column is filled from the map; period_in_window is always 'unknown (map)'.

placement.rule: If check G1 is possible on a sheet, coordinates are computed from the map's own printed Palestine grid: the published tile position is corrected by a similarity fit of tile positions to nominal grid intersections in the window (or the sheet's G1 mean offset if fewer than 3 intersections are in the window). Otherwise the published georeferencing is used uncorrected, and its G2 residual RMS is the position error.

georeferencing_checks.G1_grid: Where printed grid lines or grid crosses are visible, pick their intersections on the tiles (pixel picks, 1 to 3 m). Residual = tile position minus the correct WGS84 position of the nominal grid coordinate (pyproj EPSG:28191 to EPSG:4326), expressed in EPSG:28191 metres (dE, dN, |d|). Report per sheet: n, mean vector, median and max |d|, and the RMS about the mean. This tests the published georeferencing against the map's own frame.
georeferencing_checks.G2_ground: Independent controls: (a) the W2B grid_convert.py CONTROLS that fall on these sheets (NEAEHL grid references, about 100 m rounding); (b) places_v2 rows with sigma_km <= 0.1 whose feature the map shows; (c) up to 4 sharp features per sheet that exist on both the map and Esri imagery (building corners, spring houses, monasteries), chosen for identifiability before any residual is computed. Residual = map position (published, and after the G1 correction) minus the reference position, in metres. Each residual carries the reference's own sigma.
georeferencing_checks.G3_reference_points: kohlit_chain/reference_points.json candidates have no surveyed coordinates. They enter only through the Tell es-Sultan registration below, with Esri reference coordinates.
georeferencing_checks.C3_vector_overlay_QA: Optional: compare my name readings and positions with the 1940s vector overlay for windows outside the protected zone. Report agreement counts and position differences. Not used as data.

toponym_flags.label: INFERENCE; no identification claim
toponym_flags.rule: Flag a name if its consonantal skeleton, after normalisation (k/q/kh and h/ḥ kept distinct where printed, vowels dropped), contains one of the roots below in order. Report every flag; a flag says only that the root is present.

roots.scroll: places_v2 'asla' (project place for a scroll name)

toponym_flags.context_flag: Also flag, as 'context', names printed inside the Buqeiʿa and Qumran windows that earlier project records tie to Achor or Sekakah (Buqeiʿa, Sumra/Samra, Mird, Abu Tabaq, Qumran). Context flags are not root matches.

compare: SWP sheet XVIII (1880) positions already in places_v2 ('PEF XVIII, georeferenced')
Esri World Imagery 2025 viewed at z17 to z19

states.built_over: the position (with its error) lies inside continuous modern buildings or paving
states.destroyed_or_cut: a modern quarry, road cut, earthwork or reservoir covers the position
states.visible_2025: a matching feature is visible at the position within its error
states.open_not_visible: open ground, no matching feature visible; unknown, not absent

landscape_change.landscape_items: Also record, once per window, the presence in 1940s and 2025 of: refugee camps (ʿAin es-Sultan, ʿAqabat Jabr), settlements, main roads, quarries, reservoirs.
landscape_change.swp_rule: For each places_v2 row georeferenced from SWP XVIII whose name the 1:20,000 also prints, report the distance between the two positions; both are label or symbol positions with their errors.

tell_es_sultan_protocol.applies_to: Any view of sheet 19-14 tiles, the vector overlay, or Esri imagery that covers the protected zone.
order: 1. Register SULTAN-1-precamp-mouth from chain.json (copied verbatim) in a declaration file under research/assessments/kohlit_chain/registrations/, and record its SHA-256 and UTC time in README.md, before any 19-14 view.
2. Fill the capture form (research/shared_tools/cli.py capture) in scratch; keep a copy of the CSV row in my folder.

3. The declaration names: document, transform (similarity), target relations (mouth_10m, north_sector), control candidates, the check-point rule, the target frame and reference source, the mask, and a secondary exploratory grid fit.

4. Coarse preview: the 19-14 window at 8 m per pixel with the mask painted solid. Choose the check point on it: RP-SPRING if the map shows the spring outside the mask; otherwise the eligible candidate nearest to the zone that the map shows.
5. Pick controls at full resolution (2 m per pixel) on masked mosaics only. Pick reference coordinates on masked Esri mosaics.
6. Write the section-8 record, hash it, record the time, then run registration.py and save its output.
7. Only then view the zone at full resolution, and code what the map prints there with the measured error.

zone_nominal_grid.basis: WBADB E334 192150/142050 (50 m) and the places_v2 Wikidata point 192181/142115; the strip runs from the tell's north foot to about 250 m north

mask_grid.placement: the mask is placed in the tile frame by adding the mean G1 tile offset measured on sheets 19-13 and 18-14 (or, if none, the union of zero offset and the index-box offset), plus a further 50 m on every side

controls_declared: RP-TAWAHIN (only if the map labels the mills, as the identity check)
RP-ABU-HINDI (only if the map labels it)
RP-ROADS (only a junction on an unchanged alignment)
tell_es_sultan_protocol.secondary_fit: Exploratory: a similarity fit of printed grid intersections outside the mask (target = nominal grid coordinates, error 0 in the map frame) with the same withheld check point. registration.py would refuse grid points as unlisted, so this fit calls its fit_similarity function directly and is labelled exploratory. It proposes, but does not add, grid candidates for reference_points.json.
tell_es_sultan_protocol.no_rescue: Controls, transform and check point are not changed after the check error is seen. Any later change is a new exploratory registration.

tests: registration record passes registration.py validation (status not 'invalid')
limits: a 1:20,000 symbol cannot date a feature
